review_comments.body:
**Invalid string IDs now raise ValueError subclasses, not TypeError** · correctness This applies when `delete`, `forget`, `activity_log`, `get_import` or the group methods get a non-numeric or empty string such as `"abcdefgh"` or `""`. `path_id` raises `InvalidIdError` or `EmptyIdError`, and both subclass `ValueError`, so the old `TypeError` no longer comes out. The existing test `tests/subscribers_test.py::test_given_invalid_subscriber_id_when_calling_delete_...` runs `pytest.raises(TypeError)` on `delete("abcdefgh")` and will now fail. Callers that catch `TypeError` also stop catching these errors. Every docstring still says `:raises: TypeError`. Meanwhile `get` and `update` still raise `TypeError` for the same inputs, so the class is inconsistent. The new tests hide this: the ID-only test accepts any of the three exception types. **Suggested fix** Pick one behaviour. Either keep `TypeError` for these methods, for example by wrapping `path_id` and re-raising `ValueError` as `TypeError`, or deliberately switch to the new exceptions. In the second case, update the existing test in `tests/subscribers_test.py` and the `:raises:` docstrings, and make `get` and `update` consistent.
Prompt for a coding agent ``` In mailerlite/sdk/subscribers.py, the methods delete, forget, activity_log, get_import, assign_subscriber_to_group and unassign_subscriber_from_group now call path_id, which raises EmptyIdError/InvalidIdError (ValueError subclasses) for bad strings. The existing test tests/subscribers_test.py::test_given_invalid_subscriber_id_when_calling_delete_then_returning_subscirber_will_fail expects TypeError and will fail. Either keep TypeError for these methods, or update that test and the `:raises:` docstrings to document EmptyIdError/InvalidIdError. Keep get/update consistent with whatever is chosen. ```

## Confidence Score: 5/5 **[Low risk]** The change widens subscriber ID inputs from int to digit-only strings, reusing the existing path_id and _ID_PATTERN validators, so invalid values are still rejected before any request is sent and integer and email inputs keep their behavior. The review read only the diff and not mailerlite/sdk/_params.py, so the exact validator semantics are unverified, but nothing in the diff suggests a defect there and the new tests cover the rejected and accepted cases. ## Findings
Earlier findings (1 resolved) - [`mailerlite/sdk/subscribers.py:184`](https://github.com/mailerlite/mailerlite-python/blob/20a43437360bbab23836187f9ce60fb3e769f6a2/mailerlite/sdk/subscribers.py#L184) [Invalid string IDs now raise ValueError subclasses, not TypeError](https://github.com/mailerlite/mailerlite-python/pull/111#discussion_r4527203341) · correctness · resolved
### Summary Subscriber methods accept numeric string IDs while still raising TypeError Subscriber methods now validate IDs through the shared `path_id` helper, wrapped in `_subscriber_id`. That wrapper converts the helper's `EmptyIdError` and `InvalidIdError` (both `ValueError` subclasses) to `TypeError`. `get` and `update` use the digit pattern directly. The new mock-based tests assert `TypeError` and that no request is sent. **What's good** - The `_subscriber_id` wrapper keeps the existing TypeError contract and chains the original error with `from error`. - Tests cover edge cases such as a trailing newline, non-ASCII digits, booleans and an empty string, and check that no HTTP request is made.
Review context · 0/5 commands · 1 overlapping pull request - **Commands run:** none - **Also open:** - [#106](https://github.com/mailerlite/mailerlite-python/pull/106) changes `mailerlite/sdk/subscribers.py`
Reviews (2) · Last reviewed commit: ["test: enforce subscriber TypeError contr..."](https://github.com/mailerlite/mailerlite-python/commit/6070ed0190c905e2b9798d9f8eb02a526b27b223) · claude-sonnet-5-5

Thanks for catching the exception compatibility regression. The subscriber-only ID methods now translate the shared validator's ValueError subclasses to TypeError, preserving the documented exception contract while still accepting numeric string IDs. Tightened the existing offline regression tests to require TypeError for empty and malformed IDs, including both subscriber and group arguments, and removed the duplicate suite; the targeted run passes 11 tests and 128 subcases without HTTP calls.

This comment was drafted with Claude Code.

Closing this, but the bug is real: the API returns IDs as strings and the SDK rejects them with `TypeError` before any request is sent. Thanks for reporting it!

The PR fixes one module out of nine. Groups, segments, fields, forms, webhooks, campaigns, automations and ecommerce keep the same `isinstance(x, int)` check, and in `subscribers.py` itself `ecommerce_stats` and `ecommerce_orders` are still int-only on current `main`.

The `_subscriber_id` wrapper is the other problem. `path_id` raises `EmptyIdError` and `InvalidIdError`, both `ValueError`, and that is the contract `emails.py` already exposes. Converting them back to `TypeError` means `emails.get("abc")` and `subscribers.delete("abc")` fail with different exception types for the same mistake.

We will fix this in one PR: `path_id` across all resources without wrapper, tests in the existing per-resource files.
